model.name: Alias / Same-as Mapping
model.purpose: Federated identity equivalence with authority and confidence: record, qualify and safely publish cross-authority assertions that two identifiers refer to the same subject, together with the strength, asserting authority, confidence and evidence of each assertion.
model.scope_statement: WM-XCT-036 is a mixin that any model carrying identifiers can adopt to record and publish equivalence assertions between identifiers held by different authorities. It owns the assertion itself (recorded relation strength, asserting authority, confidence, evidence, lifecycle), the recorded canonical preference and cluster membership derived from those assertions, and the complete export and projection contract by which assertions are rendered into file, document, tabular, linked-data, API, MCP, database and web-preference surfaces without being strengthened. It does not generate candidate equivalences, does not reason over them, and does not execute the web or database surfaces it describes.
in_scope: Alias assertions stating a directed or symmetric equivalence between two identifiers or resource references held by different authorities.
Recorded relation strength, from strict logical identity down to advisory presentational preference, with explicit non-upgrade rules.
Asserting authority, confidence value and evidence qualifiers attached to each assertion.
Recorded canonical/preferred-identifier selection and equivalence-cluster membership as asserted, non-inferential state.
Assertion lifecycle: proposal, publication, supersession, retraction and deprecation.
Export and projection of assertions into Git/file templates, Markdown, HTML, JSON, YAML, CSV, RDF, APIs, MCP-backed files or databases, MongoDB and HTTP redirect/canonical surfaces.

Deterministic serialization, schema/version self-description, content digests, machine-readable projection-loss reporting, import round-trip verification and refusal when safe weakening is impossible.
out_of_scope: Entity resolution, record linkage, similarity scoring or any algorithm producing candidate alias pairs.
OWL/RDFS reasoning, transitive closure or materialised inference over asserted equivalences.
Execution of HTTP redirects, endpoint or DNS mutation, and web-server or database administration.
Master-data merge and survivorship rules deciding which attribute value wins across aliased records.
Access-control enforcement, audit-trail storage and retention execution, owned by the adopting Dimension's platform services.
Identifier scheme definition, minting and syntax validation, owned by the identifier-scheme model.

boundary_notes.distinction: OWL 2 individual equality and SKOS mapping properties both presuppose that the identifiers being related already exist under their own schemes. This mixin therefore adds only the cross-authority equivalence assertion and its projection contract; identifier minting, scheme syntax, authority registration and single-authority identity remain with the parent entry.

SKOS declares closeMatch deliberately non-transitive to stop mapping errors compounding, which presupposes asserted and reviewed mappings rather than computed chains. This model records asserted equivalence with its evidence and never computes candidates or scores.

SameIndividual is an axiom whose entailments are computed by a reasoner. This model may project to owl:sameAs when the recorded strength permits, but closure, entailment and consistency checking stay with the reasoner.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Web publishing and HTTP serving infrastructure
boundary_notes.distinction: 3xx redirection and the canonical link relation express routing and preference over representations, and RFC 8288 forbids inferring extra semantics from a relation type's presence or cardinality. This model calculates advisory redirect and canonical maps; emitting them is owned by the serving infrastructure.
PROV-O agent, activity and derivation terms are reused as qualifiers on assertions and export activities; management of the full provenance graph remains with the provenance model.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Host storage and interface platforms (MCP servers, MongoDB deployments, Git hosts)
boundary_notes.distinction: Resource URIs, mimeTypes, subscriptions, Extended JSON modes and collection layout are defined and operated by the host platform. This model carries binding parameters and expected type fidelity only, never platform lifecycle or administration.

sources.title: OWL 2 Web Ontology Language Quick Reference Guide (Second Edition)
sources.relevance: Defines SameIndividual/owl:sameAs as individual equality and DifferentIndividuals/owl:differentFrom; sets the ceiling construct that a projection may use only for strict recorded identity.

sources.title: SKOS Simple Knowledge Organization System Reference
sources.relevance: Defines skos:exactMatch (transitive, sub-property of closeMatch), skos:closeMatch (symmetric, deliberately non-transitive), broadMatch and relatedMatch; supplies the graded mapping targets and the transitivity hazard.

sources.title: RFC 9110: HTTP Semantics
sources.relevance: Section 15.4 redirection semantics: 301/308 assign a new permanent URI, 303 redirects to a different resource; grounds the rule that redirects are routing projections, not identity proof.

sources.title: RFC 6596: The Canonical Link Relation
sources.relevance: Defines rel=canonical as the preferred IRI whose content is duplicative of or a superset of the context IRI; asymmetric and not an equivalence assertion.

sources.title: RFC 8288: Web Linking
sources.relevance: Link context, relation type, target and target attributes; IANA registration policy; explicit prohibition on inferring additional semantics from presence, absence or cardinality of a relation type.

sources.title: RFC 8785: JSON Canonicalization Scheme (JCS)
sources.relevance: Deterministic JSON serialization for hashing: I-JSON subset, lexicographic member ordering by UTF-16 code units, ECMAScript number serialization, and the IEEE 754 precision limitation.

sources.title: RDF Dataset Canonicalization (RDFC-1.0)
sources.relevance: Canonical blank-node labelling and deterministic N-Quads output enabling isomorphism testing and digesting of RDF projections independent of serialization.

sources.title: JSON-LD 1.1: A JSON-based Serialization for Linked Data
sources.relevance: @id, @context, term definitions, IRI expansion/compaction and lossy compaction; grounds identifier conversion, self-description and non-guaranteed round-trip in linked-data projections.

sources.title: Model for Tabular Data and Metadata on the Web
sources.relevance: Annotated tabular data model, cell/column annotations, metadata discovery precedence, and the explicit statement that the model cannot distinguish an empty unquoted from an empty quoted field.

sources.title: Model Context Protocol Specification: Resources
sources.relevance: Resource URI, name, title, mimeType, size, text vs blob contents, URI templates, annotations and subscription/list-changed capabilities; defines the MCP-backed projection surface and what the server, not this model, owns.

sources.title: MongoDB Extended JSON (v2)
sources.relevance: Canonical vs relaxed modes and the specific BSON types (Int32, Int64, Double, Date) that lose type fidelity in relaxed mode; grounds declared type-fidelity loss for database projections.

sources.title: Shapes Constraint Language (SHACL)
sources.relevance: Validation report structure (sh:conforms, sh:ValidationResult, sh:focusNode, sh:resultPath, sh:sourceConstraintComponent, sh:resultSeverity) reused as the shape of projection conformance and loss reporting.

sources.title: RFC 9530: Digest Fields
sources.relevance: Content-Digest vs Repr-Digest scope, the registered hash algorithm registry, and the explicit statement that digests detect corruption but do not provide authenticity.

sources.title: PROV-O: The PROV Ontology
sources.relevance: prov:Entity, Activity, Agent, wasGeneratedBy, wasDerivedFrom, wasAttributedTo and qualified forms; supplies the provenance stamps carried by each projection.

sources.title: RFC 3339: Date and Time on the Internet: Timestamps
sources.relevance: Mandatory seconds and mandatory UTC offset or Z in date-time values; grounds the separation of assertion event time from export generation and re-import observation time.

sources.title: schema.org property: sameAs
sources.relevance: Defines sameAs as the URL of a reference web page that unambiguously indicates the item's identity, not as an identity axiom; the canonical weak-projection target and a documented misreading hazard.

sources.title: YAML Ain't Markup Language (YAML) version 1.2, Revision 1.2.2
sources.relevance: Representation graph, anchors and aliases as serialization-level node identity, tag resolution, and the explicit discarding of key order, anchor names and presentation detail on composition.

sources.title: JSON Schema: A Media Type for Describing JSON Documents (draft-bhutton-json-schema-01)
sources.relevance: $schema as dialect declaration, $id as canonical base URI, $ref resolution and vocabularies; grounds the self-description requirement on JSON-family projections.

bundles.name: Projection surfaces and deterministic form
bundles.description: What alias assertions may be rendered into, how each target is described as a versioned capability profile, and how output is made byte-stable, self-describing and digestible.
bundles.rationale: Export semantics cannot be stated without a per-target capability declaration: constructs, qualifier slots, identifier forms, cardinality and metadata mechanisms differ sharply between RDF, tabular, document, MCP, database and HTTP surfaces. Only canonicalized, self-describing output can be compared, digested or re-imported, so determinism belongs with the surface definitions rather than with fidelity reporting.

layers.name: Projection targets and binding
layers.description: Capability profiles for each supported target, the distinct semantics of web-preference surfaces, and the binding parameters for record, document, interface and database projections.

findings.name: Projection target capability profile
findings.description: A named, versioned declaration of what a projection target (Git/file template, Markdown, HTML, JSON, YAML, CSV, an RDF serialization, an HTTP API, an MCP resource, a MongoDB collection, or an HTTP redirect/canonical surface) can express: which relation strengths it can carry, which qualifiers have native slots, which identifier form it requires, what cardinality and ordering it guarantees, and which specification defines its metadata and typing mechanism. Nothing may be projected into a target that has no resolvable profile.

findings.name: Web-preference projections: redirect, canonical link, HTML and RDF links
findings.description: Binding rules for rendering alias assertions onto HTTP 3xx redirection, the canonical link relation, HTML link markup and RDF link predicates. These surfaces express routing or editorial preference, not identity: 301 and 308 assign a new permanent URI, 303 explicitly points at a different resource, and rel=canonical designates a preferred IRI whose content is duplicative of or a superset of the context IRI. RFC 8288 additionally forbids inferring further semantics from a relation type's presence, absence or cardinality. Output is an advisory map handed to the serving infrastructure.

findings.name: Record, document, interface and database bindings
findings.description: Binding parameters for projecting assertions into structured records: JSON and YAML documents, CSV rows under a CSVW metadata description, HTTP API payloads, MCP resources with uri, name, mimeType and text or blob contents, and MongoDB documents in canonical or relaxed Extended JSON. Covers identifier conversion, cardinality flattening of multi-valued qualifiers, and type fidelity, including the Int32/Int64/Double collapse in relaxed Extended JSON and YAML implicit tag resolution. A database view, secondary key or YAML anchor is a storage or serialization convenience with no assertional force.

findings.inline_only_rationale: The binding is a compact set of reference parameters carried on the projection request and echoed in the loss report: target record shape, field map, identifier conversion rule, Extended JSON mode and MCP resource template. The emitted documents, collections and resources are named, stored and served by the host platform, so this model holds only the parameters and the declared type-fidelity expectation. Materialising a separate binding artifact would duplicate the versioned capability profile already governed under als-proj-target-profile and would create two places where the same target could drift.

layers.name: Deterministic form, self-description and integrity
layers.description: Byte-stable serialization, content digests as integrity qualifiers, and the schema, version and provenance declaration every projection must carry to be interpretable without out-of-band knowledge.

findings.name: Deterministic serialization and content digest
findings.description: Rules producing byte-stable output so that two exports of the same assertion set are comparable and digestible: JCS for JSON-family output, RDFC-1.0 canonical N-Quads for RDF datasets, explicit row and column ordering with normalized quoting for tabular output, and fixed UTF-8 encoding with fixed line endings for Git, Markdown and HTML templates. YAML anchors, aliases and implicit tag resolution are suppressed because they are discarded on composition. The resulting digest is recorded as an integrity qualifier using a registered algorithm; it detects corruption, is not proof of authenticity or truth, and is never the artifact's identifier.

findings.name: Schema, version and provenance self-description
findings.description: Every projection carries a self-description block: the dialect or context identifier appropriate to the target ($schema for JSON-family output, @context for JSON-LD, a CSVW metadata descriptor for tabular data, mimeType and annotations for MCP resources, front matter for Git templates), the model version, the target-profile version, the strength-mapping-table version, and provenance stamps naming the producing agent and the derivation from the source assertion set. All times are RFC 3339 values with seconds and an explicit offset, and the assertion's event time is kept distinct from the export generation time and any later observation time.

findings.inline_only_rationale: The declaration is a header block that must live inside whichever artifact the target format already defines: a $schema or @context member, a CSVW metadata descriptor, an MCP resource mimeType with annotations, or Git file front matter. Extracting it into a separate artifact would destroy the self-description property it exists to provide and would let the header drift from the bytes it describes. It is therefore modelled as inline reference data present on every projection rather than as an artifact of its own.

bundles.name: Semantic preservation, loss disclosure and round-trip
bundles.description: Rules that keep a projection from asserting more than its source, the machine-readable disclosure of everything the target could not carry, and the verification and refusal behaviour that follows.
bundles.rationale: Targets differ in expressive power, so every export is a weakening or an annotation. The contract is trustworthy only if strengthening is structurally impossible, every omission is declared in a typed report, re-import is verified against canonical forms, and the failure mode when no safe weakening exists is refusal rather than silent misstatement.

layers.name: Relation-strength preservation
layers.description: The governed mapping from recorded strength to permissible target construct, and the invariant that projection may weaken or annotate but never strengthen.

findings.name: Relation-strength mapping and the non-upgrade invariant
findings.description: A governed table binding each recorded strength to the strongest construct each target may use, under a hard invariant: a projection may weaken, annotate or omit, never strengthen. SameIndividual and owl:sameAs assert individual equality and are permitted only where a competent authority recorded strict identity. skos:exactMatch is transitive and a sub-property of skos:closeMatch, while skos:closeMatch is symmetric and deliberately non-transitive, so a chain of close matches must never be projected as exact matches. schema.org sameAs is defined as the URL of a reference page indicating identity, not as an identity axiom. Confidence values, evidence records, cluster membership, canonical preference and redirect targets remain qualifiers; crossing a confidence threshold is not an upgrade.

layers.name: Projection-loss disclosure
layers.description: The typed, machine-readable report that accompanies every projection and states exactly what the target could not carry.

findings.name: Machine-readable projection-loss report
findings.description: Every projection emits a loss report enumerating, as typed entries: omitted qualifiers, unsupported relation kinds together with the substitute construct used, cardinality changes such as multi-valued qualifiers flattened to one column, identifier conversions and their reversibility, hidden evidence present in the source but invisible in the target, ordering changes, and non-round-trippable fields. The report follows the SHACL validation-report shape: a top-level conformance or fidelity verdict plus a list of entries each carrying a focus reference, a path, a component identifier and a severity. An empty report is a positive claim of losslessness for the declared profile, not the absence of a report.

findings.description: Re-importing a projection and comparing the reconstructed assertion set with the source through the same canonical form and digest. Results are classified as byte-identical, semantically equivalent, weakened as declared, or divergent. Declared loss already listed in the loss report is reconciled and discounted; anything else is undeclared loss and is a defect. Round-trip never repairs strength: a re-imported close match is not evidence that the source was strict identity, and compaction in linked-data or relaxed database modes may legitimately fail to reconstruct the original form.

artifacts.identity_strategy: Authoritative master-system verification identifier where the store issues one; otherwise a governed report IRI derived from the projection IRI plus a monotonic run sequence; otherwise a Dimension-minted UUID or ULID. The run sequence never encodes a date.

findings.name: Partial projection and refusal when safe weakening is impossible
findings.description: When a target cannot express any construct at or below the recorded strength without misrepresenting it, the correct outcome is partial projection of the safely representable subset, or refusal. Typical triggers: a target whose only equivalence construct asserts individual equality while the assertion is a graded close match; a redirect surface that would imply permanent replacement for a merely preferred alias; a canonical link whose asymmetry contradicts a symmetric assertion; or an access label barring emission. The outcome is a calculated recommendation with reasons. It does not enforce anything: the adopting Dimension decides, executes and records any override.

findings.inline_only_rationale: A refusal is a decision record returned by the evaluation function and carried as fields on the projection attempt and, where a partial projection was released, in its loss report. There is no document to publish because nothing, or only a declared subset, was exported. Enforcing the refusal, storing the decision in an audit trail and applying any override are performed by the adopting Dimension's platform services, so materialising an artifact here would claim ownership of enforcement and audit-trail semantics this model does not hold.

Requested profile version, or a request for the current version

composition.purpose: Specialise the parent identity surface with cross-authority equivalence assertions and their projection contract. Identifier minting, scheme syntax, authority registration and generic identity lifecycle machinery remain in the parent and are not restated here.

composition.target: Host entity, event, resource or agent models that carry identifiers
composition.purpose: Attach alias assertions and projection bindings to any identified subject without altering the host's own identity, attributes or lifecycle.
Strict-identity projection target, permitted only where the recorded strength is strict identity from a competent authority. Entailment, closure and consistency checking remain with the reasoner.

composition.target: SKOS mapping properties: exactMatch, closeMatch, broadMatch, relatedMatch
composition.purpose: Graded mapping targets for non-strict strengths, carrying the declared transitivity of exactMatch and the deliberate non-transitivity of closeMatch as constraints on projection.
Weak reference-page projection target; emitted only with an explicit non-identity note because the property denotes a reference page indicating identity rather than an identity axiom.

composition.target: IANA canonical link relation (RFC 6596), Web Linking (RFC 8288) and HTTP redirection semantics (RFC 9110)
composition.purpose: Web-preference projection targets. This model calculates advisory redirect and canonical maps and carries their non-identity semantics; emitting responses, mutating endpoints and serving configuration remain with the infrastructure owner.

composition.target: RDF Dataset Canonicalization (RDFC-1.0) and JSON Canonicalization Scheme (RFC 8785)
composition.purpose: Deterministic serialization algorithms bound per target format so that projections are comparable, digestible and round-trip verifiable.

composition.target: JSON-LD 1.1, W3C Model for Tabular Data, and JSON Schema draft 2020-12
composition.purpose: Linked-data, tabular and JSON-family projection targets, supplying identifier compaction, metadata description and dialect declaration mechanisms; their lossy-compaction and syntactic-indistinguishability limits are carried as declared loss.

composition.target: MCP resource interface (Model Context Protocol, resources)
composition.purpose: Carries resource URI or template, name and mimeType binding parameters only. Server capability negotiation, subscriptions, list-changed notifications and resource lifecycle remain with the MCP server.

Carries the canonical or relaxed mode selection and the resulting type-fidelity expectation for database projections. Collection layout, indexing, storage administration and deployment operation are not owned here.

Supplies the report shape reused for projection conformance and loss reporting: a conformance verdict plus typed results with focus, path, source component and severity. Execution of a SHACL processor is not owned here.

Supplies the registered digest algorithms used as integrity qualifiers and the agent, activity and derivation terms stamped on each projection. Verification, signature policy and management of the wider provenance graph belong to their owning services.

owner_package_requirements: Name an owner for the projection target profile set and for the relation-strength mapping table, and publish the version of each that governs any released projection.
Declare which store and interface act as the system of record for projection artifacts, loss reports and round-trip reports, and whether that store issues authoritative master-system identifiers.
Supply the access labels, retention schedule and audit sink that projections depend on; this model consumes those decisions and defines none of them.
Register any locally added target profile with a capability class and a citation to the specification that defines the target's constructs, so that alignment claims stay falsifiable.
dimension.namespace_guidance: Projection, profile and report identifiers live under a namespace the adopting Dimension controls and can serve; profile and mapping-table identifiers are scoped to the model namespace WM-XCT-036. Identifiers are never minted under an alignment target's namespace such as OWL, SKOS or schema.org, and terms borrowed from external vocabularies are referenced by their published IRI and never redefined locally. Where a projection is published as linked data, the declared context must resolve and must not silently rebind an external term.
registry_links: IANA Link Relations registry, for any relation type named in a web projection, under the RFC 8288 registration policy.
IANA Hash Algorithms for HTTP Digest Fields registry, for the digest algorithm named on a projection; only algorithms with Active status are used for new output.
The adopting Dimension's own registry entry vr.wm-xct-036, for the model version cited in each projection self-description header.

canonicalization_rules: JSON-family projections are canonicalized with the JSON Canonicalization Scheme: I-JSON subset, lexicographic member ordering by UTF-16 code units, ECMAScript number serialization. Values exceeding IEEE 754 double precision are carried as strings and the substitution is declared as a loss entry.
RDF projections are canonicalized with RDFC-1.0 to canonical N-Quads before digesting, so that blank-node labelling and statement order do not affect the digest.

Tabular projections declare row ordering by an explicit sort key over stable identifier columns, fix column order in the metadata descriptor and normalize quoting. Because the tabular model cannot distinguish an empty unquoted field from an empty quoted field, a syntactic-fidelity loss entry is always emitted.

Text-template projections for Git, Markdown and HTML fix UTF-8 encoding, LF line endings, no trailing whitespace and a declared front-matter key order. YAML output omits anchors and aliases and uses explicit tags rather than implicit resolution, because serialization-level node identity and key order are discarded on composition and would otherwise destabilise the digest.
patch_rules: A released projection is never edited in place. A change to the source assertions, the governing profile or the mapping table produces a new projection version carrying a supersession pointer and a new digest.

Target profiles and the strength-mapping table change additively, with explicit deprecation. A mapping entry is never silently retargeted to a stronger construct; raising a permitted construct requires the steward's recorded decision and a specification citation.
Loss reports and round-trip reports are append-only per projection version. A correction is issued as a new report that references and supersedes the earlier one, which remains readable.
compatibility_rules: Adding a qualifier slot, a target profile or a loss-entry type is backward compatible. Removing one, or narrowing a permitted construct set so that an existing mapping changes meaning, is a breaking change requiring a new model version in the projection header.
A consumer that does not recognise a loss-entry type must treat the projection as of unknown fidelity rather than as lossless.
A projection that omits its dialect, model version, profile version or mapping-table version is rejected as uninterpretable and is never processed under assumed defaults.

identity_priority: Authoritative master-system identifier issued by the system of record for the projection artifact, profile or report, wherever such a system exists.
Governed global identifier or IRI from a namespace the adopting Dimension controls and serves, used when no master-system identifier exists.
UUID or ULID minted by the adopting Dimension, used only as a last resort and never derived from a date, a content digest or an export sequence number.
artifact_rules.timestamp_rule: All timestamps are RFC 3339 date-time values that include seconds and an explicit numeric offset or Z. Assertion event time (when an equivalence was asserted, superseded or retracted) is recorded separately from projection observation or ingestion time (when an export was generated, re-imported or verified); where the two differ, both are carried and the drift interval is derivable. Timestamps are metadata and never serve as identifiers or version labels.
artifact_rules.serial_naming_rule: Serial artifacts, namely target profiles, canonical projection packages, loss reports and round-trip reports, are named as artifact-kind, subject identifier and a zero-padded monotonic sequence, for example projection.<subject-id>.v0007. The sequence is monotonic per subject and never encodes a date, digest, byte count or wall-clock ordering. Human-facing labels may display the generation timestamp, but the identifier and its sequence remain independent of it.
artifact_rules.integrity_rule: Every released artifact carries a content digest computed over its canonical form, naming an algorithm with Active status in the IANA Hash Algorithms for HTTP Digest Fields registry and stating whether the covered scope is representation data or transferred content. The digest is an integrity qualifier that detects corruption; it is not proof of authorship, not proof that the projected assertions are true, and never the artifact's identifier. Where authenticity is required, a separate signature is taken over the same canonical bytes and recorded alongside, not in place of, the digest.

policies: Non-upgrade policy: a projection may weaken, annotate or omit a recorded relation, never strengthen it. Confidence values, evidence records, cluster membership, canonical preference and redirect targets are qualifiers and are never emitted as strict identity in any target, and no confidence threshold converts a graded assertion into an identity axiom.

Full-disclosure policy: no projection is released without an accompanying machine-readable loss report. An empty report is an explicit claim of losslessness for the declared profile, not the absence of a report.

Self-description policy: every projection declares its dialect or context, model version, target-profile version, strength-mapping-table version, canonicalization algorithm and digest, so that it is interpretable without out-of-band knowledge.

Advisory-surface policy: redirects, canonical links, RDF links and database aliases produced here are recommendations to the owning infrastructure. This model calculates and reports them and never executes, deploys, mutates or administers them.

Refusal-over-misstatement policy: where no construct at or below the recorded strength exists in the target, the projection is reduced to the safely representable subset or refused, and the reason is recorded with its specification citation.

read: Read a target profile, the strength-mapping table, a projection artifact, its loss report and its round-trip reports by identifier and version.
Read the canonical bytes and recorded digest of a released projection for independent verification without re-running the export.
Reads honour the projection's inherited access label: restricted loss-report entries are withheld while the report envelope, fidelity verdict and entry counts remain readable.
create: Create a target profile only with a capability class, a citation to the specification defining the target's constructs, and a named steward.
Create a projection only from a plan that passed the non-upgrade invariant check; creation emits the canonical package, its digest and its loss report as one indivisible release.
Create a round-trip report only when the stored projection and the re-imported assertion set both reduce to a comparable canonical form.
update: Released projections are immutable; an update produces a new version carrying a supersession pointer and a new digest.

Target profiles and the strength-mapping table are updated additively with explicit deprecation; any update that raises a permitted construct requires the steward's recorded decision and a specification citation.
Corrections to a loss or round-trip report are issued as superseding reports; the superseded report remains readable so that earlier consumers can reconstruct what they were told.
delete: Projections are deleted by supersession and withdrawal, not erasure: a withdrawn or expired projection is marked withdrawn and retained as a tombstone carrying the artifact identifier, canonicalization algorithm, digest, schema and profile versions, withdrawal reason and RFC 3339 withdrawal time, so that downstream consumers can detect that a previously published projection is no longer authoritative.

Hard deletion of exported bytes, storage reclamation, backup expiry and legal-hold handling are executed by the adopting Dimension's retention policy together with the host store (file system, Git repository, MongoDB deployment, MCP server or serving infrastructure). This model records the disposition decision, its justification and its effective time, and never performs or enforces the deletion.

Deleting or withdrawing a projection never deletes or weakens the underlying alias assertion. Assertion retraction is governed by the model's assertion lifecycle, and a withdrawn projection must not be read as evidence that the equivalence was false.

Tombstones for withdrawn redirect or canonical projections record only the advisory removal recommendation; removing the live 3xx response, Link header or canonical element is performed by the serving infrastructure that owns the origin.

Loss reports and round-trip reports are retained for at least as long as the projection version they describe, so that a tombstoned projection can still be explained; their disposal follows the same Dimension-owned retention schedule.

roles.name: Projection Steward
responsibilities: Maintain and version target capability profiles and the relation-strength mapping table.
Approve any change that would raise a permitted construct, recording the specification citation and any dissent.

roles.name: Export Producer
responsibilities: Run the planning, canonical serialization and loss-report calculations for a requested scope.
Ensure every released projection carries its complete self-description, digest and loss report.

roles.name: Import Verifier
responsibilities: Perform round-trip verification against stored projections and classify the fidelity state.
Escalate undeclared loss as a defect against the profile or the producing function rather than adjusting the source assertions.

roles.name: Standards Alignment Reviewer
responsibilities: Check that each alignment claim cites a resolvable specification and version, and record conflicts where sources disagree.
Reject conformance claims that lack evidence, including claims that a target construct is equivalent to a recorded strength.

roles.name: Dimension Data Owner
responsibilities: Set access labels, publishability, retention schedule and audit sink for projections.
Decide on refusal overrides and accept the recorded risk, with execution handled by the Dimension's platform services.

access.default_rule: Projection definitions are readable by any agent authorised to read the Alias / Same-as Mapping model. Generated projection artifacts inherit the most restrictive access label of any alias assertion they contain and are never published more widely than their least-public input; where labels conflict, the most restrictive prevails and the restriction is declared in the loss report.
exceptions: A projection whose inputs include restricted or personal identifiers may be exported only under a redacted profile that omits the restricted identifier, with the omission recorded as a loss entry.
Public web projections such as redirects, canonical links and HTML markup are limited to assertions explicitly labelled publishable; an absent label is treated as not publishable.

Emergency read of a withheld projection follows the adopting Dimension's break-glass procedure; this model records only the request parameters and a reference to the outcome, not the authorisation decision itself.

Internal-only loss entries, such as those naming withheld evidence sources, are suppressed from published reports while the entry count and maximum severity remain visible so that consumers know the report is incomplete.
audit_requirements: Each released projection supplies producer identity, target profile identifier and version, strength-mapping-table version, canonicalization algorithm, content digest and RFC 3339 generation time with seconds and offset.
Every refusal, partial projection or override supplies the triggering condition code, the loss-report reference and the deciding role.
Every round-trip verification supplies the compared digests, the fidelity state and the observation time, distinguished from the export generation time.

Audit entries are written to the adopting Dimension's audit service. This model specifies the fields to be supplied and owns neither the storage, the retention nor the tamper-evidence of the resulting trail.

read_order: AGENTS.md, for the model name, type and the four resolvable URLs, read first regardless of whether the model is stored as files, in MongoDB or behind an MCP server.
Specification URL, for the model boundary, bundles, layers, findings and the non-upgrade invariant.
Storage type URL, for how projections, loss reports and round-trip reports are persisted, versioned and tombstoned in the adopting store.
Interface URL, for the read, calculate, validate and report operations exposed and the fact that no operation executes or mutates a target surface.
Processes URL, for projection planning, refusal and override handling, round-trip verification and withdrawal procedures.

coverage.claim: These bundles specify the export and projection contract of the Alias / Same-as Mapping mixin: how recorded equivalence assertions are rendered into Git and file templates, Markdown, HTML, JSON, YAML, CSV, RDF, APIs, MCP-backed files or databases, MongoDB and HTTP redirect or canonical surfaces without strengthening any relation, and how the resulting loss is declared, digested, validated, round-trip verified or refused. Every construct-level rule is grounded in a named W3C, IETF or first-party format specification with a version. Assertion authoring, candidate generation, inference and enforcement are governed elsewhere and are treated strictly as inputs or as owned by the adopting Dimension.

checklist.notes: Profiles, projections and reports use master-system identifier first, then a governed IRI, then a Dimension-minted UUID or ULID. Digests are integrity qualifiers only, serial labels are monotonic sequences, and no identifier carries a date component.

Projections are immutable once released and change by supersession, withdrawal and tombstoning; withdrawal never implies the underlying equivalence was false. Profile and mapping-table changes are additive with explicit deprecation.

The strength-mapping table binds each recorded strength to the strongest permissible construct per target, enumerates forbidden pairs, and carries the transitivity properties of exactMatch and closeMatch as explicit constraints.
RFC 3339 with seconds and explicit offset throughout, with assertion event time, export generation time and re-import observation time kept as distinct fields and the drift interval derivable.
PROV-O agent, activity and derivation stamps are carried inside each projection's self-description; management of the wider provenance graph stays with the provenance model.

Named stewards own target profiles and the strength-mapping table. Serving infrastructure, host stores and MCP servers retain ownership of execution, storage and administration, recorded as boundary notes and reference links.

Conformance results follow the SHACL report shape and cover profile conformance, self-description completeness and the non-upgrade invariant, with the offending constructs enumerated rather than merely counted.

Projections inherit the most restrictive label among their inputs; public web surfaces require an explicit publishable label, and suppressed loss entries still expose counts and maximum severity so incompleteness is visible.

Withdrawal-by-tombstone with mandatory retained fields is defined here; byte erasure, storage reclamation, backup expiry and legal hold are executed by the adopting Dimension's retention policy and the host store.

Bindings to OWL 2, SKOS, schema.org, JSON-LD, CSVW, JSON Schema, YAML, MCP, MongoDB Extended JSON, RFC 6596 and RFC 9110 are recorded as versioned alignments, with each specification's own stated limits carried as declared loss.
JCS and RDFC-1.0 canonicalization plus registered Active digest algorithms; destabilising format features are suppressed and listed, and residual instability is disclosed rather than hidden.
Four fidelity states, declared-versus-undeclared loss reconciliation against the loss report, and an explicit rule that round-trip never repairs or raises a relation's strength.
Candidate generation, similarity scoring and entailment closure are outside the model boundary; projections carry only asserted relations, and no function performs matching or reasoning.

Redirect execution, endpoint mutation, store administration and audit-record storage belong to the adopting Dimension and the owning infrastructure; this model supplies fields, recommendations and reasons only.

Content digests detect corruption but not authorship, and the specification cited says so explicitly. No signature suite, key management or trust-anchor profile has been selected for published projections, so authenticity is currently an unmet requirement rather than a solved one.

known_omissions: No profile is defined for RDF-star or RDF 1.2 triple terms, so qualifier attachment in RDF currently relies on named graphs or sidecar records, both of which are declared as cardinality or hidden-evidence loss.
Signature and key-management profiles for published projections are unselected; only content digests are specified.

Format coverage stops at the listed targets. Spreadsheet binary formats, Parquet and Arrow, GraphQL schema projections and SQL DDL views are not profiled and must not be projected until a profile exists.
Streaming, incremental and delta projections are not modelled; every projection is treated as a complete snapshot of its declared scope, which makes large federated exports expensive.

Internationalisation of literal qualifiers, specifically language tags and base direction, is only partially addressed through the tabular and linked-data alignments and has no dedicated loss-entry type.

The registry records a parent entry but no relation rationales, so the composition targets listed here are proposed alignments awaiting registration rather than ratified contracts; the parent EXTEND link in particular should be treated as a gap until its rationale is recorded.
conflicts: skos:exactMatch is declared transitive while skos:closeMatch is deliberately non-transitive to stop errors compounding. Projecting a chain of close matches into exactMatch would silently manufacture transitivity the source never asserted, so this pairing is a forbidden mapping.

schema.org defines sameAs as the URL of a reference web page that unambiguously indicates the item's identity, not as an identity axiom, yet consumers routinely treat it as owl:sameAs. Projections to it must therefore carry an explicit non-identity note.

RFC 9110 treats 301 and 308 as assigning a new permanent URI while 303 explicitly redirects to a different resource. Tools that harvest redirects as equivalence conflate these, so redirect observation is never accepted as evidence of identity here.

RFC 6596 permits the canonical target to be a superset of the context IRI's content, making the relation asymmetric. It therefore cannot be projected back as a bidirectional alias, which conflicts with common site-migration practice.

MongoDB relaxed Extended JSON collapses Int32, Int64 and Double distinctions that canonical mode preserves. A relaxed export cannot be round-trip verified at type level and must declare that loss explicitly.

YAML anchors and aliases denote node identity within one serialization and are discarded on composition, yet naive exporters emit them as if they expressed sameness; the canonicalization rules suppress them for this reason.
JSON-LD compaction is acknowledged as lossy by its own specification, so a compacted linked-data projection cannot be claimed round-trippable without also publishing the context that governed it.
regional_assumptions: No jurisdiction-specific rules are assumed. Where an identifier is personal data, the adopting Dimension's applicable data-protection regime governs whether it may appear in any public projection at all, and that decision precedes every rule stated here.

Public web projections assume the adopting Dimension controls the origin serving the context IRI. Where it does not, redirect and canonical output is a recommendation to a third party with no expectation of adoption.
UTF-8 is assumed throughout. Legacy regional encodings in CSV or Git-tracked files require an explicit transcoding step that must be declared as an identifier conversion and a fidelity loss.
Calendar and numeric formatting in human-readable projections follows the target profile, not a locale default; no regional formatting is inferred from the consumer's location.
adversarial_checks: Attempted to justify emitting owl:sameAs for a high-confidence probabilistic match once a threshold was crossed. Rejected: SameIndividual asserts individual equality, and no confidence value converts a graded assertion into an equality axiom. The threshold non-upgrade flag exists to make this refusal auditable.

Tested whether a chain of 301 responses could be projected as transitive identity. Rejected: RFC 8288 forbids inferring extra semantics from a relation type's presence or cardinality, and RFC 9110's 303 demonstrates that redirection can target a genuinely different resource.

Tested whether a content digest could serve as the projection's identifier, which would be convenient and stable. Rejected: digests detect corruption rather than establish authenticity or identity, and two unrelated exports of the same empty scope produce the same digest.

Checked whether the loss report should own storage of the audit trail or enforcement of refusals, since it already knows the facts. Rejected: the report is a derived record, and audit-trail and enforcement semantics belong to the adopting Dimension's platform services.

Considered importing entity-resolution scoring so projection could select targets automatically. Rejected: matching produces the assertions this model consumes, and modelling it here would duplicate a sibling model's function and blur the asserted-versus-computed boundary.

Checked whether a CSV projection could ever be declared lossless. Rejected: the tabular data model itself cannot distinguish an empty unquoted field from an empty quoted field, so every CSV projection must carry at least a syntactic-fidelity loss entry.

Tested whether a database view, secondary key or YAML anchor could stand in for an alias record and save a projection step. Rejected: each is a storage or serialization convenience with no asserting authority, no strength and no confidence, and reading one back as an assertion would fabricate provenance.

Reviewed whether the advisory redirect map amounts to owning redirect execution. Rejected: the map is a calculated, non-executing recommendation carrying an explicit advisory-only flag, and every function's effects statement excludes writing to endpoints, repositories, collections or serving configuration.
